newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia chasing wheat sales to India, Egypt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia chasing wheat sales to India, Egypt.

text.p: Australia is pursuing further sales of wheat to India and Egypt, Alex Nichol, spokesman for the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), said on Wednesday.

Nichol was responding to reports that India was in the market for 50,000 tonnes or more of optional-origin wheat for March arrival, expected to be drawn from either Australia or the United States, and trade suggestions that Egypt was seeking a further 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
"We would always go for any market. Yes we would be interested in that. We've got a big crop to sell and we're interested in anyone who wants to buy," Nichol told Reuters.
India was happy with the last Australian wheat sale and the AWB would certainly like to do more business, he said. Whether it did or not would probably depend on price, he added.
The AWB announced in December that it had sold one million tonnes of Australian Standard White to India for January/February delivery at A$185.00 a tonne FOB.
Nichol on Wednesday confirmed a sale of 110,000 tonnes of hard wheat to Egypt for February/March delivery, but would not comment on price, which has been reported at US$190.00 a tonne.
The AWB shipped 373,726 tonnes of wheat last week, bringing total shipments for the year beginning October 1 to 5.173 million tonnes, up from 3.824 million tonnes a year before.
The AWB would ship more than two million tonnes in the current month "no trouble at all", Nichol said.
